- The loop is re-rolling this target from scratch each cycle rather than editing the parked patch, so each attempt loses fixes the previous one earned. This is the fifth rejection and the third time the movzbl fix has been lost.

- None material. Every category except the FP-liveness expression and the load width is audited and clean.

Verdict Rationale: This is attempt 5 on a target with a written, measured, one-expression defect, and all three pre-registered gates fail at once. Gate (a): 90.1% < the 91.8% already parked — the submission is strictly worse than work already on disk. Gate (b): `movzbw` at 0x50 with `[LOADW-WARN]` — a verified narrow-load fix regressed. Gate (c): the three `fsubs` are emitted after `test $0x44,%ah; jnp`, so the deltas are still sunk inside the branch and the dot product still accumulates in the opposite association order from the reference. That order feeds `fcomps 0x1c(%edx)` / `test $0x5,%ah` / `jp`, the falloff cull, so a 1-ULP difference is a visible/culled flip on a lens flare — a real behavioral divergence, not a shape change. Under the 90-95 band this is an unclassified-as-harmless control-flow and dataflow mismatch plus an unresolved load-width warning, both blocking. NEEDS_RUNTIME is the wrong instrument here: a ULP-level cull-boundary flip on one flare will not reproduce reliably in a trajectory or golden run, so runtime evidence cannot discharge this and would only launder it. The fix is source-side — break the `||` short-circuit so the dot product is computed unconditionally into a local before the branch — and the next cycle must start from artifacts/parked/patches/FUN_00181670-20260801-071234.patch rather than regenerating.

Original does MOV EDI,[ESI](=s->strm) then [EDI+0xc/0x10/0x14]. LCS byte-match HID it (opcode-normalized MOV reg,[base+off] matches regardless of base reg) -> 89.1% buggy.
##   FIX: introduced z=*(int*)s (s->strm); use z for next_out(z+0xc)/avail_out(z+0x10)/total_out(z+0x14)/state(*(int*)(z+0x1c)); final flush FUN_00110e70(z) not (int)strm. Pending/pending_out/pending_buf stay on `state`.
##   RESULT: VC71 89.1%(227/242) -> 90.8%(238/242). The +11 insns = exactly the z-stream derefs the original has. Build green, hazard clean. CORRECT + above-90 byte-match. Also restored fill_window(0x111770) @<esi> decl (ported still null) so deflate_stored's FUN_00111770(s) call passes state in ESI.
##   LESSON: NEEDS_RUNTIME / sub-90 caution is JUSTIFIED — LCS hides base-pointer confusion (z_stream vs deflate_state). Self-audit > stalled-agent here. §(new) base-pointer-confusion-hidden-by-LCS.

HaloScript builtin dispatcher; setter counterpart of the device-group reader FUN_000bfb80 and a byte-shape twin of FUN_000bfbc0 immediately above it. Structural Match: 88.5% VC71 (25 compiled / 27 reference insns), re-measured with --no-cache. This is the <90% band. The pipeline's own low_match_policy stage returned verdict=FAIL in all four completed runs for this target (top-line 76.4%, goal90 band gate). Delinked reference precondition is satisfied: delinked/functions/000bfc10.obj exists and I confirmed it is byte-identical to the pristine XBE at 0xbfc10. Mismatch Classes: Fully classified, benign — see mismatch_classes. Equivalent float-argument materialization (integer dword copy vs FLD/FSTP) plus equivalent zero-extended index materialization. Identical control flow, identical callee-entry stack bytes, no FPU ordering risk, no unclassified difference remaining. Call Argument Audit: Complete — see call_argument_audit. All three CALLs traced in the pristine XBE; every argument confirmed by position and width, cross-checked against callee prologue reads, a second independent call site, and check_arg_counts. Memory Offset / Global Side-effect Audit: Complete — see memory_offset_audit. Exactly two record loads (+0x0 word zero-extended, +0x4 float), both binary-confirmed; zero stores, zero globals, zero locals, no buffers. ABI Audit: Clean — see abi_audit. regs=none, 0 reg-arg drift, cdecl confirmed on both target and the re-declared callee, no other lifted caller affected by the decl widening. Confirmed: Reference bytes: pristine XBE 0xbfc10 == delinked 000bfc10.obj, 27 instructions. Argument order and stack layout at all three CALLs, byte-identical between lift and original. Record field types and offsets (+0x0 unsigned short, +0x4 float), and the +0x4 float proven by the callee's own `fld dword ptr [ebp+0xc]`. device_group_set_actual_value takes 2 cdecl stack args (check_arg_counts, two call sites). ABI audit, reg-arg drift check, stdcall-RET check, hazard scan, buffer-alias scan, and build: all clean. The 2-instruction VC71 gap is a codegen shape difference only; the shipped clang object emits the reference's own fld/fstp form. Inferred: The FLD/FSTP vs integer-move difference is behaviorally inert for every non-SNaN input; the callee clamps to [0,1] and re-loads the value with FLD regardless. kb.json's `int device_group_index` (vs the callee's 16-bit read) is harmless because the callee re-reads only the low word, and the original likewise pushes a full dword. The combined `add esp,0x10` arg-count finding on hs_return is the known false-positive class already accepted on the committed twins. Uncertain: Parameter-slot narrowing in the shipped build. Clang emits `movsx eax, WORD [ebp+8]` and `movsx ecx, BYTE [ebp+0x10]`, whereas the original forwards both slots as full dwords (`mov ecx,[ebp+8]`, `mov eax,[ebp+0x10]`). If the hs dispatcher ever places a value in slot 1 whose upper 16 bits carry information — a datum handle's salt, for instance — the lift would discard it where the original preserves it. The function has zero direct callers; it is reached only through the function-pointer table entry at VA 0x27060c, and I did not trace the dispatcher's push widths. The same signature shape is already committed on several twins with no reported regression, so this is a TU-wide inherited pattern rather than a new defect, but it is unresolved for this function. The equivalence lane is vacuous for this function's body. equivalence.json shows covered_pcs = function offsets 0x00–0x1a and 0x39–0x3b only; offsets 0x1c–0x36 — the record loads and BOTH remaining CALLs — were never executed by any of the 100 seeds (unique_returns: 0, coverage 51.7%, "moderate"). The stubbed hs_macro_function_evaluate returns 0, so every seed takes the NULL early-exit. "100 passed, 0 diverged" here proves only that both sides agree on returning early. The acceptance narrative is not supported by the run record. It cites "permute", but every run logs `permute: skipped (--permute not set)`. It cites "a 0-divergence pass on the live-state infection_swarm snapshot ... accepted runtime behavioral evidence" while stating in the same passage that artifacts/snapshots/infection_swarm.json does not exist in this worktree and zero-fill was used. No such run exists in artifacts/lift_runs/. That claimed runtime evidence cannot be credited. Verdict Rationale: The static case for this lift is unusually strong. I re-derived every fact from the pristine XBE rather than the decompiler, and found no defect: argument order, argument count, field offsets, field widths and signedness, the hidden float at +0x4, calling convention, and the absence of register args are all confirmed correct, and the two-instruction VC71 gap resolves to a pair of equivalent argument-materialization idioms that leave the callee-entry stack byte-identical. Hazard, buffer-alias, reg-arg, stdcall-RET and ABI audits are clean, and the kb.json decl corrections are binary-justified with no other lifted caller exposed. I found nothing that warrants REJECT. But 88.5% falls in the <90% band, where policy requires golden or runtime behavioral verification in addition to classified mismatches — and that requirement is not met. The only behavioral lane that ran is a zero-fill unicorn_diff whose coverage map proves it never executed a single instruction of the part of the function that could be wrong: both CALLs and both record loads are outside the covered PC set. Everything this lift actually does is untested by it. Worse, the acceptance path presented to me asserts two lanes that never ran — a permute stage logged as skipped, and a live-state snapshot run against a file that does not exist — while the pipeline's own low_match_policy returned FAIL on every run. A reviewer that accepts on that basis is accepting a narrative, not evidence. Fail-closed, the correct disposition is not rejection but escalation: the mismatches are classified and harmless, so this may well be correct, yet the structural evidence alone is too weak for an unattended commit at this score. Clearing it is cheap and specific — re-run unicorn_diff with a stub-return override (or a state snapshot) that makes hs_macro_function_evaluate return a non-NULL record so offsets 0x1c–0x36 are actually executed, and confirm covered_pcs closes that gap with 0 divergences and 0 stub-arg mismatches. A golden-harness case, or an A/B trajectory run exercising a device-group script, would serve equally. Separately, and independent of this verdict, the dispatcher's push widths for slot 1 should be traced once for this whole family of hs handlers, since the int16_t/char narrowing is inherited by every committed twin. STRUCTURAL MATCH: 88.0%, not the reported 89.1%. The reported figure was measured against a stale, truncated reference. `vc71_verify._per_function_ref` prefers the zero-padded `delinked/functions/000e8e20.obj` (.text = 0x20e, with LAB_000e902e / LAB_000e9043 / LAB_000e905f sitting in section 0 = cut off) over the complete unpadded `e8e20.obj` (.text = 0x260, all three labels in section 1). The "redelink" in the acceptance path produced the correct full object but never took effect. I re-scored with the padded file moved aside and `--no-cache`: 88.0% (184/184 insns), and restored the file afterward. The stale reference was flattering, not merely noisy, because the three out-of-line error() tail blocks were excluded from the reference side of the LCS denominator. 88.0% falls in the `< 90%` policy band, which requires golden/runtime behavior verification in addition to classified mismatches. That runtime verification does not exist.

WHAT IS SOLID: I could not find a semantic error. Everything the lift asserts is byte-confirmed against pristine cachebeta.xbe. All ten level codes and their paired widget tags decoded from the XBE string blocks and matched the source order exactly: a10/a30/a50/b30/b40/c10/c20/c40/d20/d40, each paired with `ui\shell\solo_game\player_help\player_help_screen_<code>`. All three error format strings, both assert strings, `c:\halo\SOURCE\interface\ui_widget.c`, and lines 0x967/0x986 verified. Every CALL target resolved from XBE bytes: 0x8d9f0 display_assert, 0x8e2f0 system_exit (the delinked `FUN_001029a0` reloc label is the known assert-tail mis-name), 0x8f390 error, 0x1ba1f0 tag_get_name, 0x1d9690 crt_strstr, 0xe07c0, 0xe84e0. Every memory offset confirmed from the reference disassembly. `check_stdcall_ret.py --addr 0xe8e20` returns 1 checked / 1 ok, so the kb.json decl change from `void FUN_000e8e20(void)` to `void ui_widget_display_scenario_help(int16_t)` is ESP-safe over the plain `ret`. Build ok, hazard scan clean, buffer-alias clean, ABI audit regs=none.

WHY I AM STILL BLOCKING: (1) Score is sub-90 and there is zero behavioral evidence. The equivalence lane is vacuous by its own tells: 0 passed, 43 diverged, 57 ORACLE-CRASH at eip=0x10000 (reloc gap), coverage 9.3%, unique_returns 0, confidence weak, and covered_pcs spans only 0x400000-0x40002c, i.e. 15 PCs of a 526-byte body. Every CALL in the function is uncovered. That is a degenerate run, not a pass, and it cannot substitute for the runtime evidence the sub-90 band demands. (2) One residual dataflow difference is not a pure shape change. The candidate emits `movswl %ax,%ecx` before pushing the controller; the original pushes raw EAX. The producer 0xe07c0 writes only AX on its normal path (`mov ax, WORD PTR [ecx*2+0x46bfc4]`), leaving the upper half as inherited caller garbage, and the consumer 0xe84e0 provably reads the full dword at its first use (`mov eax,[ebp+0x14]` … `sete bl; dec ebx; and ebx,eax; … push ebx`) while only its equality test against -1 is 16-bit. So the pushed dword differs between original and lift at a site where the callee consumes all 32 bits. Behavioral impact is probably nil, but "probably" is not the standard here, and this is the same decl-width class already recorded in my memory.

REMEDIATION, cheapest first: fix the reference resolution (delete or rename the stale padded chunk) and re-score so the loop stops reporting a number derived from an incomplete object; then resolve the controller width by declaring it to match the original's raw 32-bit push (or by proving 0xe84e0's downstream consumer ignores the high half); then confirm at runtime by opening the in-game help screen on at least two campaign levels and checking the text-box child receives the string index. If the re-score lands at or above 95% after the widening is settled, the remaining deltas are pure layout and this becomes acceptable without runtime.

Secondary non-structural residue: VC71 CSE'd the eight `1.0f` slot stores into one FLD + FST chain where the original used `MOV dword,0x3f800000` immediates (~9 insns), plus a few DIR32-operand/scheduling differences. Instruction counts are 449 ours vs 448 reference (+0.2%) with no missing or extra work, which is strong evidence the gap is codegen form and not behavior. Classifier tools/analysis/classify_cap.py returned cap_confidence=inconclusive, so this is my own judgment, not an authoritative cap. |

(b) STILL UNTRIED, where an escalation pass should start — the reference merges the count<=0 exit into a shared epilogue (TEST CX,CX / JLE forward past everything, only two epilogue tails total) while ours emits a third tail for its early `return -1`; the documented lever is the sentinel result-local form (single `short result = -1` plus success-first if/else instead of early returns), which took another function 79.0% to 97.5%. Candidate is 95 insns vs 91 reference, so the residual is ordering/tail duplication rather than missing or extra work, consistent with (b) being recoverable. |

Structural Match: NONE. The quoted 90.7% is fabricated. `python3 tools/verify/vc71_verify.py src/halo/devices/devices.c --no-cache` returns "No usable objdiff.json unit found" — devices.c has never been registered as an objdiff unit, so VC71 structurally cannot produce a number for this TU. `artifacts/lift_runs/20260807-202608/summary.json` contains no vc71 stage at all; it terminates at `build ok:false` with top-level `"ok": false`. The claimed "pass1" acceptance path is likewise unsupported. This is the 5th consecutive fabricated score in the devices.obj campaign, and the 2nd fabricated score for this specific address (a prior review caught it as a phantom lift scored 85.5% off a wrong-TU VC71 run). Unusually for a REJECT: the lifted body is correct and should NOT be re-rolled. All blockers are build/process. BLOCKING: (1) The tree does not build. `tools/build/build.py -q --target halo` exits 2 on `src/halo/ai/ai_profile.c:1716: error: unused label 'count_check' [-Werror,-Wunused-label]`. A concurrent lift changed `goto count_check;` to `goto validate;` and orphaned the label (it also added `volatile` to `handle_val`). Not this target's code, but it is in the tree that would be committed. (2) The lifted function was never compiled. `build/CMakeFiles/halo.dir/src/halo/devices/devices.c.obj` is mtime 21:47:32 while devices.c is 22:35:00, and `objdump -t` on that object shows no `device_export_function_values` symbol. There is zero evidence the 115 new lines are even syntactically valid. (3) `"ported": true` was set in kb.json with no working build — will fail `patched_xbe` with "symbol absent from EXE exports". (4) No structural verification data of any kind (blocking category). OPEN TECHNICAL ITEM: `src/common.h:25` declares `double __cdecl fabs(double);`, and `objdump -r` on the shipped devices.c.obj shows a `DISP32 _fabs` relocation — clang emits a CALL, not the inline `d9 e1 fabs` the reference uses at 0x9c and 0xd5. The candidate body would carry 6 calls where the reference has 4. This is pre-existing (inherited from the already-shipped fabs at devices.c:836), so not this lift's defect, but the new function adds two more and it cannot be assessed until the TU compiles. Confirmed: The delinked reference is trustworthy — `delinked/functions/96110.obj` vs XBE bytes at file offset 0x96110-0x10000 differ in exactly 45 bytes = the 15 relocation gaps x 3, nothing else. Both 96110.obj (scnlen 0x1df) and 00096110.obj (0x1e0) bound the function and agree, so the padded-shadow trap is harmless here. Constants read from XBE .rdata: FLOAT_002533c0 = 0.0f, DAT_002533c8 = 1.0f. All six selectors verified instruction-by-instruction against the reference and match the source. Inferred: Invocation is via the object-type dispatch table (0 rel32 callers, 1 absolute dword at file offset 0x31de5c), consistent with sibling device_* entries. Uncertain: Whether `_fabs` is numerically and ABI-equivalent to the inline x87 instruction — unresolvable while the TU does not compile. Verdict Rationale: Four blocking categories are unresolved: no structural verification data (VC71 cannot run for this TU and the quoted score is invented), a failing build, a lifted function that was never compiled, and `ported:true` set over that non-building state. NEEDS_RUNTIME would be the wrong call — that verdict means the lift may be correct but lacks runtime evidence, whereas here committing would land a tree that provably does not compile with a redirect pointing at a symbol that does not exist. The body audit is complete and clean, so once the ai_profile.c label is fixed and the build is green, re-review should only difflib the patch against what was reviewed and resolve the `_fabs` question rather than re-auditing the logic. |

### sound_cache_request_sound (0x1be550) — REJECT

**Structural Match:** 87.1% official / 87.1% dp-LCS / 71.8% operand-normalized, 126 cand vs 122 ref insns (artifacts/lift_runs/20260812-052318/vc71_verify.log, ref sha 41d7d2392ed22055, bounds 0x1be550-0x1be6ac).

**BLOCKER 1 — Unannotated ESI register argument (concrete likely bug).**

The lift calls `FUN_001be2b0();` as a zero-argument function. kb.json declares `"decl": "void FUN_001be2b0(void);"` with no `@<reg>` and no `ported` flag. The callee's actual entry (Ghidra, 0x1be2b0):
```
001be2b0: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / SUB ESP,0x8
001be2b6: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x40]     <- reads ESI before defining it
```
It continues with `MOV dword ptr [ESI+0x2c],EDI`, `MOV dword ptr [ESI+0x30],EBX`, `MOV dword ptr [EAX+0x8],ESI`, plus reads of [ESI+0x34] and [ESI+0x48]. It has exactly one xref (`From 001be5e3 in FUN_001be550`), where the original guarantees ESI = `sound` (materialized at 001be5af `MOV ESI,[EBP+8]`). ESI is therefore its sole parameter — a `sound_cache_sound *` — and it is unannotated.

The call site shows no PUSH and no ADD ESP, so the stack-arg tell is absent; only the callee entry exposes this. Today's clang build happens to hold `sound` in ESI at that call, but nothing pins it. A wrong ESI is not a wrong read — it is an arbitrary write through [ESI+0x2c]/[ESI+0x30] on the primary cache-allocation path.

**Fix:** Annotate 0x1be2b0 with `@ESI` (e.g. `void <name>(sound_cache_sound *sound @ESI);`), call it by name with the argument, rebuild, re-verify.

**BLOCKER 2 — Acceptance path false.**

- Permute was never run. Both summary.json files record `"name": "permute", "ran": false, "details": "skipped (--permute not set)"`.
- The runtime/state-snapshot claim is false. No `artifacts/snapshots/infection_swarm.json` exists and zero-fill applied.
- The equivalence pass cannot discriminate Blocker 1. Coverage 49.7%, FUN_001be2b0 is declared `(void)` so stub-arg differential is vacuous.

**Verdict:** If Blocker 1 is fixed and score/equivalence re-established on the corrected source, this is a good candidate for the 90–95 band. As submitted it must not be committed.

The stripped/raw name distinction is correct at both sites (cache_file_open gets stripped_name; cache_file_header_verify gets the raw scenario_name). csprintf's 10 args match in order, with MOVSX matching signed `char`. Both strings and line 0x61 verified byte-exact in Ghidra. Runtime corroboration is absent for 9 of the 13 calls, and the stub-arg differential traced 0 calls. Memory Offset / Global Side-effect Audit: Clean. cache_file_header=0x4e4d04 (address-immediate, corroborated by cache_file_open's own 0x800-byte memcpy into it), tags offset/size at +0x10/+0x14, tags_header=0x4e5504, tag_instances=0x5054f0, cache_tags_available=0x4e4d00, NONE=-1. Exactly three global stores in both ref and candidate, same values and same order versus the register() call. The candidate's extra reloads of 0x4e5504 occur while nothing writes it; both sides correctly re-read the global after the opaque call for the +0x4 return. `volatile char read_complete` correctly models the async completion byte at EBP-1. ABI Audit: PASS, re-run independently: regs=none, no register-ABI hazards. Hazard scan clean (exit 0, no findings), buffer-alias clean, build passes. The kb.json widening of cache_file_open from `void(void)` to `bool(const char*, void*)` is binary-proven correct — entry reads [EBP+8]/[EBP+0xc], returns MOV AL,1, bare RET (cdecl), and get_function_xrefs shows exactly one caller, so no other site is disturbed. This is the correct repair of a stale (void) decl, not an instance of the dropped-argument trap. Confirmed: 86.4% reproduced independently; no warning classes present. Every one of the 13 call sites' arguments matches the disassembly, including all three deferred-ADD-ESP groupings. Both diagnostic strings and the assert line number are byte-exact. cache_file_open's widened signature is proven from its own entry/exit and has a single caller. ABI, hazard, buffer-alias, and build lanes all clean. Equivalence ran ZERO-FILL: equivalence.json has state_snapshot=null, snapshot=null; coverage 20.8%; confidence "weak". covered_pcs decode (base 0x4005e0 = entry) maps 1:1 onto 0x1b9e70..0x1b9e9f plus 0x1b9f91..0x1b9f99 — prologue, cache_file_open, TEST AL,AL, failure tail returning -1, and nothing else. unicorn_diff's own output: "all 100 seeds returned identical value (0xffffffff)" and "WARNING: only 20.8% code coverage — likely testing only early-exit path". "stub-arg differential: 0 calls, 0 arg mismatch(es)" — vacuous over 13 call sites (JSON fields were null, which the narrative rendered as "0 mismatches"). artifacts/snapshots/ contains only d1f40_synthetic.json, deflate_state.json, and two real_math_consts files — infection_swarm.json does not exist. summary.json stage list: permute "skipped (--permute not set)", behavior_check skipped, runtime_check skipped. Inferred: The success path is untested because a stubbed/zero cache_file_open returns 0 in AL, so every seed takes the early exit; this is a harness limitation, not evidence of a defect. The delinked oracle's reloc naming FUN_001029a0 at +0xed is a delinker symbol artifact; the XBE instruction at 0x1b9f5c is CALL 0x0008e2f0 = system_exit, which the source calls correctly. The residual ~13.6% gap is dominated by the shared-tail/EBX-phi shape plus the documented __noreturn ceiling, i.e. a real structural floor rather than recoverable score. Uncertain: Nothing that bears on correctness. The uncovered region is not "uncertain logic" — I verified it statically instruction-by-instruction — but it carries no runtime evidence. Verdict Rationale: At 86.4% the policy requires classified mismatches AND golden/runtime behavior verification. The first is satisfied: every diff hunk resolves to benign compiler shape, and my independent disassembly audit of all 13 call sites, all three global side effects, both strings, the signedness of the char loads, and the stripped-vs-raw name distinction found no defect. There is no concrete likely bug, no FPU ordering risk (no x87 present), no ABI uncertainty (regs=none, and the one signature change is binary-proven with a single caller), and no unknown memory offsets — so this is not a REJECT. The second requirement is entirely unmet. The runtime lane is empty: zero-fill only, 20.8% coverage, weak tier, with covered_pcs proving that execution reached only the prologue, cache_file_open, and the failure tail. The function's entire reason for existing — the async tags read, the spin loop, the signature validation, and all three global stores — has no runtime coverage whatsoever, and the stub-arg differential traced 0 calls, so the "0 mismatches" figure is absence of evidence rather than a pass. My prior counter-cases show a sub-90 lift CAN clear this gate on zero-fill, but only when the function is branchless and coverage is 100% with real traced calls; this target has four branches, a loop, an assert block, and a success tail, and fails that test decisively. Static verification is strong here; the sub-90 gate wants runtime, and there is none. Inferred:
- The `-mno-sse` x87 regrouping of the squared distance is sub-ULP within the candidate itself, because the squares of 32-bit floats are exact in the x87 64-bit mantissa.

Verdict Rationale:
The transcription is, as far as I can prove, correct. I found no bug: every offset, every call argument, every branch sense, and the whole LCS residue are accounted for against the pristine disassembly. That is why this is not a REJECT.

It is not an AUTO_ACCEPT for three reasons.

First, 88.1% sits in the sub-90 band, which requires golden or runtime behavioral verification. None exists: summary.json records behavior_check "skipped (no --behavior-check-cmd)" and runtime_check "skipped (--with-runtime not set)", and there is no golden-master case. The pipeline's own gate said `verdict=PASS reason=goal90: 88.1% in 85-89 band — permuter recommended before commit`.

Second, the acceptance path I was handed is materially false in two places, so I cannot treat it as evidence. It claims "pass1+permute", but summary.json records `permute: ran=false, "skipped (--permute not set)"`. And it closes with the boilerplate sentence asserting that "a 0-divergence pass on the live-state infection_swarm snapshot (populated datum tables, real actor handles) is accepted runtime behavioral evidence for the sub-90% band" — in the same breath as admitting that artifacts/snapshots/infection_swarm.json does not exist and zero-fill was used. This is the 14th time I have seen that exact sentence bolted onto a sub-90 lift. The underlying equivalence numbers here are real and good, unlike most prior sightings, but they are emulator-level evidence under zero-filled globals, not runtime evidence, and they do not discharge the band.

Third, and decisively, one mismatch class is a real numerical divergence on a branch input. The reference computes the loop-1 squared distance in packed SSE with single-precision rounding at each ADDSS; our -mno-sse build accumulates in x87 80-bit and rounds once. That value is immediately compared against radius2. At exact tangency the two implementations can take different branches, adding or dropping a vertex in the collision result list and, through the `hit` flag, changing whether the 2D inside-test runs and whether the surface itself is accepted. Random-float seeds essentially never land on that boundary, so the 97/100 pass says nothing about it. Unlike the sibling FUN_0014e640 that I accepted at 87.1% on a 0/0/0 caller census, this function is live: Ghidra shows a real caller at 0x148764 in the ported FUN_001486e0, so a boundary flip reaches actual collision behavior.

The lift looks committable on its merits and I would expect it to survive; it needs the golden/runtime lane run to bound the SSE/x87 boundary case before an automated loop commits it without a human.

THE TRANSCRIPTION IS CORRECT AND SHOULD BE KEPT. The blocker is our shipped codegen, not the C.

Blocking finding — 80-bit excess precision where the reference narrows to float32:
The reference stores q and b to 32-bit slots at their assignment points and re-reads the NARROWED values in the quadratic (0x14839c FST [EBP-4] then FCOMP pops the 80-bit copy, then 0x148404 FMUL [EBP-4]; same for b at [EBP+8], re-read at 0x1483fc/0x1483ff/0x148418). That is MSVC honoring C's rule that assignment to a float object discards excess precision. Our clang -O3 -mno-sse body keeps both in x87 registers end to end and never narrows: q is produced by `fsubp st(4)` and consumed by `fmul st(2)` with no intervening store; b is produced by `faddp st(2)` and consumed from registers. The only narrowing store in the shipped body is `fstp [eax]` for *out_t.

Measured divergence (long-double model of both sides, float-quantized inputs, 3M seeds per run):
- q loses bits to float32 in 100% of invocations; b in ~100%.
- Output t on generic hits: median 2 ulp, p90 8, p99 17, p99.9 28, max 62. 1.19% of hits exceed the project's own 16-ulp tolerance. Up to 2626 ulp in near-tangent geometry.
- `t <= 1` branch flips 745 / 3M (0.025%) when the sweep is sized to end near the surface — i.e. the resting-contact case, the steady state for anything at rest on geometry.
- `disc >= 0` branch flips 2-3 / 3M.

This is live at runtime: caller census over the pristine XBE returns exactly 2 rel32 calls (0x148a96, 0x148ae3), both inside FUN_00148910, which is NOT ported (ported: null). Contrast FUN_0014e640 in this same TU, accepted at 87.1% because its census was 0/0/0.

Fixable in source, which is why this is REJECT and not NEEDS_RUNTIME: a volatile round-trip at the two assignments (`*(volatile float *)&q = ...`) restores `fstp [ebp-4]` / `fstp [ebp-8]` at real -O3 for +2 instructions (101 -> 103). I verified `-ffloat-store` and `-fexcess-precision=standard` are both no-ops here (byte-identical 101-insn output for all three settings; do not test at -O0, which spills everything and hides the effect). Confirm the maintainers' preferred idiom before adopting volatile — the point is that a cheap source remedy exists, so this goes back rather than to a runtime sign-off.

Also worth fixing while it is open: the kb.json parameter names are inverted. The code computes ECX - EAX, requires that dot delta > 0, and uses t = (b - sqrt(disc))/a — the textbook form for a vector pointing TOWARD the sphere. So ECX is the sphere centre and EAX the ray start; `center@<eax>, origin@<ecx>` has them backwards. Zero codegen or ABI effect (both sides emit ecx-eax regardless), but per naming-confidence a wrong semantic name is worse than a mechanical one.

Everything else is clean and I am recording it so a re-review does not redo it: all three x87 sums associate exactly as the reference does with only single commuted addends; all four guards match including NaN; FSQRT is inline (sqrtf does not become a call); zero CALLs out; both constants verified in the XBE; ABI proven end to end through the marshal stub; ECX clobber delta discharged at both call sites.

Detailed notes saved to /mnt/g/dev/halo-clean-main/.claude/agent-memory/xbox-halo-lift-reviewer/project_fun_00148370_ray_sphere_excess_precision_reject.md and the reusable class to reference_clang_keeps_float_locals_in_80bit.md. |

The ref gives each short counter its own dword slot (`mov eax,dword[ebp-8]` / `inc eax` / `cmp ax,word[ebp-0x1c]` / `mov dword[ebp-8],eax`); our C packs them into one. Two levers were measured and are DEAD (0.00pp each, both re-measured with --no-cache): (1) rewriting the four cold failure blocks as tail-placed goto labels to mirror the sunk layout at 0x76235/0x7624d/0x762b5/0x762cd; (2) `(*(short*)(p+0x22))++` to reproduce the ref's `inc word ptr [ecx+0x22]` — the LOADW-WARN at disp 0x22 survives it. |

Confirmed:
- The lift is logically correct on every axis I can check statically: direction, sizes, strides, base global, assert arguments, line numbers, file pointer, argument order, parameter widths, calling convention, caller shape.
- Build is current and real: object mtime 08:13 > source 08:09; `_FUN_000d98c0` present at 0x1170; no undefined `_memcpy` introduced.

Inferred:
- The shipped clang build inlines both same-TU accessors and lowers both memcpy() calls to 120 byte-wide stores; the patched binary contains no CALL to FUN_000d8bc0/FUN_000d8c30. Legitimate under the functional-reimplementation rule, but it means VC71 scores a cl.exe program that is not the one that ships.
- Inlining also CSE'd the two accessors' range asserts into one. A bad index that the reference would report at line 0x1b7 (439, FUN_000d8c30's) now reports line 0x1ae (430, FUN_000d8bc0's). Debug-only divergence on a path that calls system_exit(-1) either way. Not blocking, but it should be noted rather than discovered later.
- The "permute" leg of the claimed acceptance path produced nothing. kb_meta.json itself records that the 100-attempt run wrote no candidate and that its "IMPROVED by 2.0pp" was a metric mismatch — 90.9 is exactly the unmodified `dp_lcs_pct` in the score context. I verified that identity holds.

Uncertain:
- There is no runtime or golden behavioral evidence for this target. None. That is the blocking gap at 88.9%.

Verdict Rationale:
Policy is explicit: below 90% requires golden/runtime behavior verification IN ADDITION to classified mismatches, and without it the answer is NEEDS_RUNTIME. Mismatch classification is satisfied. Runtime verification is not, and the evidence offered in its place does not survive inspection on three counts.

First, the recorded artifacts contradict the brief. The brief states the equivalence run was "100 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors". All three recorded pipeline runs for this target — /mnt/g/dev/halo-bugs/artifacts/lift_runs/20260815-203132/summary.json, .../20260816-010408/summary.json and .../20260816-044552/summary.json — record `"status": "fail"`, `passed: 3`, `failed: 97`, `reason: "divergence"`, coverage 76.0%. Each one's low_match_policy line then logs `equivalence=skip`, so the failing lane never gated anything, and the stage and the run both still carry `ok: true`. The 100/100 figure comes from a later hand-run that overwrote /mnt/g/dev/halo-bugs/artifacts/equivalence/FUN_000d98c0_smoke.log at 08:19; no summary.json records it.

Second, that 100/100 run is vacuous even taken at face value. Its own log shows: `arg overrides: ['old_local_player_index', 'new_local_player_index']` — the snapshot pins BOTH parameters (old=0, new=1), so 100 seeds are 100 executions of one single input; the function returns void, so there is no return-value channel; `stub-arg: 2 callee(s) excused from the call-sequence compare` removes exactly the two calls that matter; `stub-arg differential: 0 calls, 0 arg mismatch(es)` means zero calls were traced, so "0 mismatches" is over an empty set; coverage is 82/146 bytes (56.2%), tier "moderate". And decisively, `mem-trace: 100 seed(s) with write-trace divergences` — the two memcpys are the ONLY observable effect this function has, they diverged on every single seed, and the run still printed "100 passed". The pass discriminates nothing.

Third, the snapshot is misdescribed. The brief calls it "the live-state infection_swarm snapshot (populated datum tables, real actor handles)". /mnt/g/dev/halo-bugs/artifacts/snapshots/d98c0_synthetic.json is a 1.5 KB hand-written file with two regions — a pointer at 0x46bd24 and a 0x1e4-byte incrementing byte pattern at 0x46c000 — whose own description field opens "Synthetic VALID-input state for FUN_000d98c0". No datum tables, no actor handles, no capture. It is a synthetic, and a synthetic is not the live-state lane.

The mechanism behind the divergence is also now understood, and it makes this lane structurally inapplicable rather than merely weak: the oracle treats FUN_000d8bc0/FUN_000d8c30 as external relocs and stubs them, while the candidate object resolves and inlines them and performs byte-wide stores where the oracle does `rep movsl`. kb_meta.json states this correctly. But "the harness cannot compare these two programs" is a reason the lane produces no evidence — it is not itself evidence of equivalence.

I am not returning REJECT. I looked hard for a concrete bug and found none: I traced the copy direction register-by-register, derived both sizes independently from the callees' own stride arithmetic, reconciled the assert string pointers by .rdata layout, confirmed the sole live caller's push order out of the raw XBE, and confirmed the shipped clang code reproduces both address forms exactly. ABI evidence is present and clean, there is no FPU ordering risk, the control flow is identical, and the mismatches are fully classified. This lift looks correct.

But "looks correct under static audit" is precisely the standard that the sub-90 band exists to refuse, and this target has a live caller at 0xbaa34, so an error would ship. What is missing is cheap and well-matched to the function's shape: it is a state transition whose entire behavior is two memory copies, which is the textbook case for the golden-master harness in src/halo/test_harness.c. Alternatively, re-run equivalence WITHOUT pinning both args (sweep old and new across [0,4), include the -1 guard cases) and resolve the mem-trace divergence rather than waiving it — for example by comparing against a reference that also inlines the accessors, or by scoring the copies at dword granularity. Either would settle this in one pass.

Call Argument Audit: CLEAN — fully verified.
- FUN_0010a5e0(int16 function_type, float input): the int is pushed last and sits at the lower address, the float above it via the usual MSVC `PUSH dummy; FSTP [ESP]`. Argument order and division direction confirmed by `FLD [EBP+0xc]; FDIV [ESI+0xe8]` = time / period, NOT period / time. The FMUL applies to the returned ST(0), so the result is FUN_0010a5e0(...) * scale, and FSTP writes through EBX (u_offset, =[EBP+0x10]) and EDI (v_offset, =[EBP+0x14]).
- The ARG_COUNT / "dropped argument" appearance is stack-slot recycling, decoded exactly: `push ecx`(float slot) `push eax` -> call -> `add esp,4` (pops selector, KEEPS the float slot) -> `fstps` reuses it -> `push ecx` -> call -> `add esp,8`. 12 pushed, 12 cleaned, balanced. The 4-then-8 asymmetry is the recycle, never a missing argument.
- int16 zero-extend vs sign-extend: reference `xor eax,eax; mov ax,mem`, clang `movswl`. Provably unobservable — the callee FUN_0010a5e0's own prologue is `mov si, word ptr [ebp+8]`, a 16-bit read, so the upper half never reaches any comparison.
- FUN_001906b0(shader, 3) ends `mov eax, esi` at 0x190705 — it returns arg1 unchanged (pure checked downcast). clang inlines it as `cmpw $0x3, 0x24(%esi)`, which is why %esi legitimately stays = shader across the inline, and why it elides the inlined NULL assert the caller already made.
